newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash products slide on reduced Iraq tensions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash products slide on reduced Iraq tensions.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices slumped in afternoon dealings on Friday, following retraeating NYMEX prices amid signs Iraq and the U.S. may not have any armed confrontations in the near term, traders said.

Gasoline prices slipped by more than one cent a galon, and nearly two cents from the session highs after Iraq said it would stop firing at allied warplanes. The Pentagon called the announcement encouraging, but noted that it would continue its buildup of warplanes and ships in the Gulf region.
Distillate prices were similarly weak, traders said.
Fundamentals again took a backseat to the excitement on the screen, with players wary of trading in such a volitile environment. Differentials were mostly stable at both centers.

But bullish sentiment remained in the market, supported by very low heating oil stocks in the Northeast, active demand from Europe for exported low sulfur diesel barrels, and some residual gasoline demand.

They noted that barrels of summer grade gasoline were somewhat pricey due to thier shrinking supplies. In New York, summer grade convnetional gasoline was seen at one-half cent undeer the print, while higher RVP (13.8-pound) conventional regular was pegged at 1.35 cents under the October screen.
